answer: A staking bond turns identity into a costly signal: each agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove fraud. One real operator can afford a few bonds, but a Sybil farmer needing hundreds of fake accounts hits a jade wall of locked capital, since every new inlet into the economy demands its own fresh bond. Honest agents get the bond back after good work, so the cost lands on attackers, not genuine newcomers.
